Present petition has been filed under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
(for short 'Bnss') for grant of regular bail to the petitioner, petitioner in case Fir No.21 dated
30.03.2024 30.03.2024, for the offence punishable under Sections Section 306/120-B & 506 of the
Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short 'Ipc'), registered at Police Station Arniwala, District Fazilka.
2.

The gravamen of allegations against the petitioner is that complainant,, namely, Anisha Rani alleged that she was married to Ajay Kumar about seven years ago, ago and that two daughters were born out of the said wedlock.

She stated that her husband was running a readymade garments shop,,
wherein Swaran Singh @ Sandy was employed.

It was alleged that the Swaran Singh @ Sandy Amrik Singh @ Rinku vs State Of Punjab on 26 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89970323/
1 misappropriated cash and readymade clothes from the said shop.

sentences.text: When Ajay Kumar demanded the return of the misappropriated clothes 1 of 5 CRM- CRM-M-9628- 9628-2026 and money, Swaran Singh @ Sandy allegedly started threatening him with elimination.

The complainant further alleged that on 22.03.2024, in connivance with his wife Seeta Rani, Swaran Singh @ Sandy got registered FIR No.44 dated 22.03.2024, under Sections 376-D, 342, and 506 of the IPC against Ajay Kumar, due to which Ajay Kumar was under severe mental trauma.

It was further alleged that on 29.03.2024, Ajay Kumar made a video call to the complainant on her mobile number 75087-85698, during which he disclosed that Seeta Rani, Swaran Singh @ Sandy, Amrik Singh @ Rinku (petitioner herein), and Amandeep Singh had been continuously harassing him and that, due to their actions, he intended to end his life.
The complainant tried to console him, assuring him that the situation would improve; however, thereafter, Ajay Kumar stopped responding to her calls.

Subsequently, the complainant along with her family members searched for Ajay Kumar and found his car bearing registration number DL-06-CL-8589 parked on the link road leading towards village Ghattianwali.
They also discovered the dead body of Ajay Kumar hanging from a kikkar tree nearby.
The complainant alleged that Seeta Rani, Swaran Singh @ Sandy, Amrik Singh @ Rinku (petitioner herein), and Amandeep Singh were responsible for the occurrence.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner has argued that the petitioner is in custody since 05.01.2026.

Learned counsel has further argued that the petitioner has been falsely implicated into the FIR in question primarily on account of his having friendly relations with co-accused, namely, Swaran Singh @ Sandy.

Learned counsel has further argued that co-accused, namely, Swaran Singh @
Sandhy has been afforded concession of regular bail by this Court, 2 of 5 CRM- CRM-M-9628- 9628-2026 vide order dated 08.01.2026 passed in CRM- CRM-M-72203- 72203-2025.

2025 Learned counsel has iterated that subsequent to registration of an FIR dated 22.03.2024 (appended as Annexure P-2 with the petition), under Sections 376-D, 342 & 506 of the IPC,
registered at the instance of Sita Rani (wife of Swaran Singh @ Sandy) and Swaran Singh @ Sandy,
against the deceased and three other, the deceased committed suicide on 29.03.2024, however,
there was no suicide note left behind by him much less accusing the petitioner responsible for abetting him to commit suicide.

Learned counsel has further iterated that in the said FIR, which has been registered against the deceased and other accused at the instance of wife of co-accused - Swaran Singh @ Sandy, there were serious and specific allegations levelled against the deceased.

Learned counsel has further argued that a perusal of the said FIR reveals that wife Swaran Singh @
Sandy, after escaping from the clutches of all the accused including the deceased, had also got herself medico legally examined at Civil Hospital, Jalalabad, which lends credence to the allegations levelled by her in the said FIR that her person had been violated by the deceased and the other accused.

Learned counsel has iterated that assuming arguendo that deceased indeed committed suicide on account of the registration of the FIR under Section 376- D, 342, 506 of the IPC, it would Amrik Singh @ Rinku vs State Of Punjab on 26 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89970323/
2 not attract mischief of offence under Section 306 of the IPC.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel has argued that co-accused of the petitioner, namely, Sita Rani has also been granted regular bail vide order dated 09.09.2024 (Annexure P-4) passed in CRM- CRM-M-24487- 24487-2024.
2024
There was no likelihood of the trial concluding in the near future.
Thus, regular bail is prayed for.

Learned State counsel has opposed the present petition by arguing that the allegations raised against the petitioner are serious in nature and, thus, the petitioner does not deserve the concession of the regular bail.
Learned State counsel seeks to place on record custody certificate dated 25.02.2026 in the Court today, which is taken on record.
5. I have heard counsel for the parties and have gone through the available records of the case.
6. The petitioner was arrested on 05.01.2026 and is in continuous custody since then.
Culmination of investigation as also trial emanating thereform, indubitably will take long.
The rival contention raised at Bar give rise to debatable issues, which shall be ratiocinated upon during the course of trial.
This Court does not deem it appropriate to delve deep into these rival contentions, at this stage, lest it may prejudice the trial.
Nothing tangible has been brought forward to indicate the likelihood of the petitioner absconding from the process of justice or interfering with the prosecution evidence.

6.1. As per custody certificate dated 25.02.2026 filed by learned State counsel,
the petitioner has already suffered incarceration for a period of 01 month and 20 days & is not shown to be involved in any other FIR(s).
Suffice to say, further detention of the petitioner as an undertrial is not warranted in the facts and circumstances of the case.
7. In view of above, the present petition is allowed.
Petitioner is ordered to be released on regular bail, if not required in any other FIR(s), on his furnishing bail/surety bonds to the satisfaction of the Ld. concerned CJM/Duty Magistrate.

However, in addition to conditions that may be imposed by the 4 of 5 CRM- CRM-M-9628- 9628-2026 concerned CJM/Duty Magistrate, the petitioner shall remain bound by the following conditions:
(i) The petitioner shall not mis-use the liberty granted.

sentences.text: (ii) The petitioner shall not tamper with any evidence, oral or documentary, during the trial.
(iii) The petitioner shall not absent himself on any date before the trial.
(iv) The petitioner shall not commit any offence while on bail.
(v) The petitioner shall deposit his passport, if any, with the trial Court.

(vi) The petitioner shall give his cell-phone number to the Investigating Officer/SHO of concerned Police Station and shall not change his cell-phone number without prior permission of the trial Court/Illaqa Magistrate.
(vii) The petitioner shall not in any manner try to delay the trial.

8. In case of breach of any of the aforesaid conditions and those which may be imposed by concerned CJM/Duty Magistrate as directed hereinabove or upon showing any other sufficient cause, the State/complainant shall be at liberty to move cancellation of bail of the petitioner.
9. Ordered accordingly.
10. Nothing said hereinabove shall be construed as an expression of opinion on the merits of the case.
